name: num_ansi_colors
title: Detect the number of ANSI colors to use

origin.description: How many ANSI colors the session should use for a stream.

arguments.name: stream
arguments.text: "auto", "stdout", "stderr", or "message". The implementation replaces this with stdout or stderr before the terminal test.

origin.details: cli.num_colors and R_CLI_NUM_COLORS win first. crayon.enabled FALSE returns 1. crayon.enabled TRUE returns crayon.colors, or 8. NO_COLOR, knitr, a sink, and a non-terminal stream return 1. A terminal then follows COLORTERM, Emacs, Windows, and tput colors. truecolor is 256^3. The requested stream is not the connection that is tested: outside a REPL the test uses stderr.

translation.description: How many ANSI colors the session should use for a stream.
translation.details: The same order as crayon. A non-interactive process is not a terminal, so the count is 1 until crayon.enabled, cli.num_colors, or R_CLI_NUM_COLORS is set. There is no R sink; options(crayon.sink_output=1) is the stand-in for an active output sink. Windows 10 build numbers come from the Windows version when the process is on Windows.
